Read this first: the raw label is spelled Infilteration (upstream CSE-CIC-IDS2018 typo, not "Infiltration"). Every table and chart in this report uses the exact raw string. Code must match it verbatim; renaming happens only via an explicit mapping at training time.

1. Dataset identity & file reconnaissance (Step 2)

1.1 What this data is

Each row is one network flow (a conversation between two hosts) described by 78 CICFlowMeter measurements: packet/byte counts, packet-length statistics, inter-arrival times (IAT), TCP flags, header sizes, window sizes, active/idle times — plus the answer column Label and capture-time columns Day, Hour, Minute, Second. One row = one training example; the 78 measurements = candidate features.

1.2 How recon was done (soul)

Binary line counting (no decoding cost), header hunt by startswith("Dst Port,"), full scan counting mid-file header repeats, byte-offset peek at head/middle/tail. Full soul code in §10.

1.3 Findings (reports/file_recon.md)

CheckResultWhy it matters
Size / lines6.22 GB / 16,137,184 linesSets chunk strategy: full load would need ~15–30 GB RAM → chunked passes mandatory on 12 GB
EncodingUTF-8 strict OKNo decoding traps mid-run
Line endingsCRLF (\r\n)Parsers handle it; raw-text audit must strip()
HeaderLine 1, 83 columns, first cols Dst Port, Protocol, Flow Duration…, last cols Label, Day, Hour, Minute, SecondFixes the schema contract every later step relies on
Mid-file header repeats0 (clean single-header merge)No daily-header pollution despite multi-day merge
Head contentPort-0 / protocol-0 benign heartbeat flows, Day 14Background class present from row 1

2. Line audit — row shapes & junk (Step 3A)

2.1 What & why

Before any numeric parsing, every one of the 16.1M lines is classified by shape alone: true-header, ok-shape (83 fields), short row, long row, terminal junk (wc -l, tail, --- paste), empty line, mid-file header. Bad rows are quarantined to rejects/rejected_lines.csv with exact line numbers. Why first: a single malformed line can shift columns or crash a chunk; shape errors must be counted exactly, never silently skipped.

2.2 Findings (reports/line_audit.csv, field_histogram.csv)

ReasonCount
ok-shape (83 fields)16,137,183
true-header1
short-row / long-row / terminal-junk / empty-line / mid-file-header0 each

Field histogram is a single spike: {83 fields: 16,137,183 rows}. The demo sample's terminal junk (wc -l, tail -n 100, separators) was an artifact of how the demo was excerpted — the full 6.22 GB file is structurally perfect. Reconciliation anchor for every later pass: parsed + dropped must equal 16,137,183.

3. Profiling pass — quality, duplicates, conflicts (Step 3B)

3.1 What & why

One sequential read in 200,000-row chunks (~150–250 MB resident). Per chunk the script audits all 83 columns (missing, non-numeric, inf, negatives, running mean/std/min/max), counts raw labels, port×label and day-hour×label joints, validates ranges, and tracks exact global duplicates via 64-bit row hashes of the features only (excluding Label so that same-flow-different-label conflicts stay detectable). A RAM guard auto-disables global dedup past 10 GB. Why: this is the only step that sees every value; everything downstream (verdict, sampling, training) trusts its counters.

3.2 Performance (logs/pass1_chunks.csv)

81 chunks in 2.2 minutes (~122,000 rows/s), RAM 0.62 GB → 2.23 GB peak — far inside the 12 GB budget, global-dedup mode stayed full throughout. Per-chunk cost was flat (~0.6–0.7 s), proving linear scaling. Duplicate accumulation was front-loaded (chunk 0 alone: +145,196 — the port-0 heartbeat flows repeating).

3.3 Row accounting (reports/duplicates_summary.csv)

3.4 Label conflicts — all one pair (reports/label_conflicts.csv)

All 6,197 conflict hashes are exactly Benign | Infilteration, 2 occurrences each. No other attack conflicts with anything. Why this happens: infiltration traffic deliberately mimics benign behaviour, so identical flow statistics legitimately occur under both labels at the class boundary. Decision (§9): quarantine all 12,396 rows (0.077% loss). Security-conservative alternative — relabel them as attack — is recorded but not applied, because it would inject 12k benign-looking flows into the attack class.

3.5 Missing / inf / non-numeric: all zero (reports/quality_table_83cols.csv)

Every one of the 83 columns has 0 missing, 0 inf, 0 non-numeric over all 16.1M rows. No imputation is needed anywhere; no had_inf flag feature is needed. This is unusual for CIC exports (which often contain Infinity strings) and means the merge was pre-cleaned or the exporter floored zero durations.

3.6 Negatives: two corruption patterns, ~1,240 rows (0.008%)

PatternColumns (count)Smoking gunVerdict
A. Timestamp jump (~14 rows)Flow Duration (14), Flow Pkts/s (14), Flow/Forward IAT Mean/Max/Min/Tot (3–14)Duration min −9.19×1011 µs (≈ −10.6 days); IAT min −8.28×1011; mirrored by giant positive max 9.8×1011Quarantine: capture-clock wraparound; all duration-derived values untrustworthy
B. int16 overflow (~1,226 rows)Tot Fwd Pkts (1,226), Subflow Fwd Pkts (1,226), Fwd Act Data Pkts (1,220), Tot Bwd Pkts (17), Subflow Bwd Pkts (17)Min −32,748, max +32,762 — straddling the signed-16-bit boundary 32,767: high-volume flows wrapped negativeQuarantine (repair by +65,536 is possible but not proven for every row; loss is negligible)
Valid sentinel (keep!)Init Fwd Win Byts: 4,432,594 × -1 (27.5%); Init Bwd Win Byts: 8,161,353 × -1 (50.6%)Exactly -1, never other negatives; marks UDP / one-way / non-TCP flows (millions of DNS port-53 + port-0 flows)Keep as a category; never impute

Why quarantine instead of repair: the union of affected rows is ~1,240 of 16.1M (0.008%). Dropping them costs nothing and removes any risk of teaching the model wrapped-clock or wrapped-counter artifacts. The 14 REVIEW columns in the verdict exist solely because of these rows — all 32 Tier-1/2 features are otherwise clean.

3.7 Constant columns → DROP (8)

Bwd PSH Flags, Bwd URG Flags + all six bulk columns (Fwd/Bwd Byts-Pkts-BlkRate Avg) have min = max (all zeros) → zero information, drop before training. Note the scale lesson: in the small demo, Fwd URG Flags, FIN/URG/CWE Flag Cnt also looked constant, but at full scale they vary (SYN floods, scans, teardowns) → kept. Never decide constancy on a sample.

3.8 Range checks: all zero (reports/invalid_ranges.csv, whole_ranges.csv)

Port 0–65535, protocol 0–255, hour 0–23, minute/second 0–59: 0 violations in 16.1M rows, independently confirmed by both the profiling pass and the whole-data pass.

4. Labels — the 15 classes (Step 4)

4.1 What & why

Raw label strings are audited for typos, case and whitespace variants, canonicalized (strip), counted exactly, and converted to imbalance ratios that later become model class weights. Port×label and day-hour×label joints are rebuilt on canonical labels. Why: the label column is the training target — any hidden variant ("Benign " vs "Benign") silently creates a phantom class.

The four ★ classes (<5,000 rows) force the family-grouping strategy in §9.

Leakage verdict: six attacks live on exactly one port (five on 80, FTP+SlowHTTPTest on 21) and SSH/Bot at 99.98%/98.4% — a port-only rule would "solve" them, then fail on any real network. Only Benign and Infilteration spread across ports (Infilteration touches 53/443/3389/80/445/135/0/22/139… — lateral movement across services, which is also why it is the hardest class and the only conflict partner). Decision: train behaviour-only; report a with-port variant purely to demonstrate the leakage gap.

Open anomaly — LOIC-UDP: all 1,730 flows target port 80 yet the label says UDP, and the flag chart (fig09) shows ACK ≈ 0.96 for this class — impossible for true UDP. Either the label names the tool mode (not the wire protocol) or these rows are mislabeled TCP. Extraction phase must print the Protocol distribution + flag means for these 1,730 rows before trusting the class.

6. Time — day/hour map & leakage proof

6.1 What & why

Joint counts of (day × hour × label) over all rows (reports/attacks_per_hour.csv, whole_label_time.csv). 15 distinct days: 1, 2, 5, 8, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 20, 21, 22, 23, 28. Why: proves whether capture time predicts the label.

Leakage verdict: six attacks occupy exactly one hour each; several (hour → attack) mappings are near-deterministic (e.g. day 16 h10 is 99.93% SlowHTTPTest). Day+Hour is a near-perfect cheat sheet. Decision: all four time columns are analysis-only and excluded from every training variant. Positive note: benign co-occurs in almost every attack hour, so time-stratified splitting is still meaningful for evaluation design.

7. Stratified sampling (Step 5A)

7.1 What & why

One more streaming pass draws a deterministic, evenly-spaced (systematic) sample per label: proportional quotas, a 1,000-row floor for mid classes, and 100% retention of classes below the floor. RNG-free (index arithmetic), fixed output data/sample_100k.parquet (+ CSV twin) reused by every chart so figures stay mutually consistent. The same pass finishes the exact label-conflict check against the duplicate hashes from Step 3B. Why sampling at all: scatter/box/correlation plots cannot render 16M points (overplotting + RAM); the sample powers shape charts while counts, ranges and histograms stay exact via the whole-data pass.

9. Verdict — training readiness & extraction rulebook

9.1 Go / no-go

GO for extraction with the rulebook below. The dataset is structurally sound (zero missing/inf/junk/range violations), fully audited row-by-row, and its leakage channels are identified and excluded. Its usable core is 15,686,859 rows × ~27 features after the column drops in §9.3.

9.2 Family strategy for the rare classes (mandatory)

SQLi (87), XSS (230) and Web (611) cannot be learned as standalone classes. Combined they give a Web-attack family of 928 flows (0.006%) — still rare but trainable with class weights ≈ benign/family ≈ 14,400:1. Recommended hierarchy: binary (Benign vs Attack) → family (DoS/DDoS, Brute-force, Web, Bot, Infiltration) → per-family tools. LOIC-UDP (1,730) keeps its own class pending the Protocol anomaly check (§5).

9.3 Column decision list (from reconciliation of §3, §5, §6, fig05)

9.4 The two open anomalies (extraction-phase checks)

  1. LOIC-UDP vs TCP: port 80 in all 1,730 flows + ACK ≈ 0.96 → print Protocol distribution and flag means for these rows.
  2. Conflicts: 100% Benign|Infilteration; default recommendation = quarantine. Alternative: relabel as attack and measure the delta.

10. Why each artifact is necessary

ArtifactWhy it must exist (what breaks without it)
file_recon + line_auditProves the parser saw every byte exactly once; without it, silent row loss (headers/quoting) corrupts all downstream counts
field_histogram (8 fields × label)Detects mid-file headers, label variants, port/garbage anomalies before any numeric parsing commits to dtypes
duplicates_summary + hashesQuantifies memorizable repetition; without global hashes, dedup is approximate and leakage into validation is invisible
label_conflictsFinds feature-identical rows with contradictory labels — untrainable contradictions that cap accuracy and must be quarantined
invalid_ranges + negatives drill-downSeparates valid sentinels (-1) from corruption (int16 overflow, timestamp jumps); decides repair vs quarantine
quality_table_83colsThe auditable per-feature certificate (missing/inf/negative/non-numeric) backing every DROP/KEEP decision
label_counts / distribution / mappingExact targets, canonical names, and class weights; identity mapping proves no hidden label variants
port_label_canonicalService map of every attack; numerical proof Dst Port is a leakage channel that must be excluded
attacks_per_hour / whole_label_timeCapture-calendar proof that Day/Hour deterministically identify most attacks → time excluded
sample_100k.(parquet|csv)One frozen deterministic sample reused by all shape charts; without it, figures would disagree with each other
whole-data pass (W1–W6)Exact counts/histograms/ranges over 16.1M rows; the only defense against sampling bias in rare classes and tails
fig00–fig10 + figW01–figW07Human-verifiable evidence of every claim; each finding in §9 traces to at least one figure and one CSV

11. Soul code — minimal logic of each step

Distilled essence (imports, logging and CLI stripped). Full runnable scripts live in steps/.

Step 1 — file reconnaissance

size = os.path.getsize(path)
enc  = detect_encoding(first_bytes)          # UTF-8-SIG check → plain UTF-8
eol  = detect_line_ending(first_bytes)       # CRLF
ncols, header = read_header()                # 83 columns
mid_headers = count_lines_equal_to_header()  # streaming compare → 0

Step 2 — line audit + field census

for line in file:                            # never loads whole file
    cells = line.split(',')
    if len(cells) != 83: junk.append(n)      # → ZERO junk rows
    else: count[cells[field], cells[label]] += 1   # 8 tracked fields

Step 3A — range & quality profiling (chunked pandas)

for chunk in pd.read_csv(path, chunksize=200_000, usecols=NUM32):
    for col in NUM32:
        s = pd.to_numeric(chunk[col], errors='coerce')
        missing[col] += s.isna().sum()       # → 0 everywhere
        inf[col]     += np.isinf(s).sum()    # → 0 everywhere
        neg[col]     += (s < 0).sum()       # → only sentinel/overflow patterns
        min[col], max[col] = min/max so far

Step 3B — global duplicate & conflict detection

seen, dup_extra, conflicts = {}, 0, {}
for chunk in chunks:
    h = hash_rows(chunk[feature_cols])       # md5 of raw row bytes
    for digest, label in zip(h, chunk[label]):
        if digest in seen:
            dup_extra += 1                   # → 437,928
            if seen[digest] != label: conflicts[digest] = {both}  # → 6,197 hashes
        else: seen[digest] = label

Step 4 — labels

raw = chunk[label].astype(str)
canon = raw.str.strip()                      # mapping = identity (verified)
counts = canon.value_counts()                # exact 15 classes
weights = counts['Benign'] / counts          # class weights

Step 5A — systematic stratified sample + conflict re-check

quota = proportional(label_counts, 100_000, floor=1000)  # rares kept 100%
pos_in_class = cumcount()                    # streaming position per label
take row if pos_in_class * quota[class] // total[class] advances  # evenly spaced
re-check each taken row's hash against Step-3B table → same 6,197 conflicts

Step 6 — charts (sample shapes + whole-data exacts)

# sample shapes: seaborn/matplotlib on sample_100k  → fig00–fig10
# whole-data exacts: chunked counters → figW01–figW07, e.g. log-grid histograms:
bin = floor((log10(x) - log10(0.001)) / step)   # 72 bins, 0.001…1e9
hist[feature, label, bin] += 1

13.2 Extraction phase (next, not part of this report)

  1. Apply §9.3 drops; quarantine 12,396 conflict rows + ~1,240 negative-pattern rows (or repair int16 with +65536).
  2. Resolve the LOIC-UDP anomaly (§5 note) and the conflict relabel-vs-quarantine choice (§9.4).
  3. Group Web+XSS+SQLi into one family (928 flows); compute exact family class weights from §4 ratios.
  4. Engineer is_header_only, byte/packet ratios, log(Duration), log(Rate); keep -1 InitWin sentinel.
  5. Emit stratified train/val/test splits (seeded) + a behaviour-only feature matrix ≈ 15.69M × ~27; report a with-port/with-time variant only as a leakage-ablation baseline.

End of report. All numbers trace to CSVs + PNGs in the uploaded bundle; no training or filtering was applied — this is the pre-training audit.
